text: Given semantic externalism, why do philosophers like Fodor introduce a notion of 'narrow content'?
choices: To argue that all content is wide and environment-dependent
To deny that mental states have any content at all
To show that Oscar and Twin Oscar differ psychologically after all
To isolate a component of content that supervenes on the subject's in-the-head state, so psychology can group Oscar and Twin Oscar together
explanation: Narrow content is the internally-determined component that Oscar and Twin Oscar share, proposed so that psychology can generalize over molecule-for-molecule duplicates despite differences in wide (referential) content. Option 0 abandons the project; option 1 is eliminativism about content; option 2 is the opposite of narrow content's motivation, since the duplicates are meant to match psychologically.
